name: From-Scratch Shio Ramen

ingredients.name: ramen noodles, either homemade or store-bought
scallions, sliced as thinly as possible

instructions.primary_message: For the Dashi: Combine kombu and shiitake mushrooms with 1 quart water in a sealable container and refrigerate for at least 8 and up to 24 hours.

Place water, kombu, and shiitakes in a small saucepan and place over medium-high heat. Bring to a bare simmer, then shut the heat off; take care not to let the water boil, as the kombu will make the dashi bitter. Add katsuobushi and let steep for 3 minutes. Strain dashi into a heatproof bowl. You can reserve the kombu, shiitakes, and katsuobushi for another use, such as making a niban dashi.

Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Combine dashi with chicken stock in a large saucepan and place over medium-high heat. Bring blended broth to a simmer; take care not to let it boil, as it will become cloudy.
Begin cooking noodles in a large pot of boiling water according to our homemade ramen noodle recipe or package instructions.

Place 2 tablespoons shio tare in each of 4 warmed serving bowls. Ladle around 1 1/2 cups blended broth into each bowl. Taste broth for seasoning; it should be quite salty. Add more broth or more tare to each bowl to adjust the seasoning.

Drain noodles and divide among serving bowls. Spoon 1 to 2 tablespoons aromatic oil over noodles in each bowl of soup. Add any toppings you have on hand, such as marinated egg or chashu, to each bowl. Garnish with scallions and serve immediately.

description: A light, clear broth and a nuanced lemon-and-salt seasoning result in a beautiful yet flavorful bowl of shio ramen.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 8 hr 35 min to 1 day 35 min.

Optional or for serving: Toppings, such as chashu or ajitsuke tamago (optional)

Optional substitutions: aromatic oil → schmaltz or lard

Notes: The aromatic oil can be made by frying aromatic vegetables, like onion, garlic, and ginger, in any kind of oil or fat, but the best type of fat for this purpose is rendered chicken fat or lard, or some combination of the two. For a detailed method for making aroma oil, consult our pressure cooker shoyu ramen recipe; if you have leftover aroma oil from that recipe, it can be used here, too.
author: Sho Spaeth
